objects.name: Sergeant Nine-Nine
objects.text: An infantry sergeant, torso and one shoulder, wedged in the stakes. His voice box crackles. 'Medics. Good. The line held. Now, orders.'

approaches.label: Stabilise him
approaches.stakes: Seal the leaks, steady the voice box. Two skills: the lower one counts, the other adds 2 if you have it.

approaches.label: Ask for his report
approaches.stakes: Who's left, who's where, and what the Colonel's last order really said.

approaches.label: Hear what he won't say
approaches.stakes: Under the jokes: what he's afraid of, and what he wants you to do with him.

objects.name: The triage line
objects.text: Twenty-three infantry robots laid in a row behind the stakes. Seven-Seven is counting. Hum is humming. Lantern holds its chest plate shut with both hands.

approaches.label: Sort who can be saved
approaches.stakes: Triage by touch and data: who can walk, who must be carried, who can't be saved.

approaches.label: Work through the pain
approaches.stakes: Your own plating is cracked. Keep your hands steady anyway.

approaches.label: Carry two at once
approaches.stakes: Every robot you can carry is one less left behind.

approaches.label: Learn their names
approaches.stakes: Serials, squads, one thing each of them cared about. Someone should remember.

objects.name: No-man's-land
objects.text: The ground between the stakes and the fallen squad. The enemy mined it before they pulled back.

approaches.label: Read the ground for mines
approaches.stakes: Find the safe way across before someone steps wrong.

approaches.label: Sprint it
approaches.stakes: Cross fast enough that nothing gets you.

objects.name: The fallen squad
objects.text: Eleven infantry robots who held the far post. Two of their lights still blink. Scavenger drones circle above.

approaches.label: Drive the drones off without a fight
approaches.stakes: Stand up, make yourself big and loud, and don't flinch when they dive.

approaches.label: Strip usable parts
approaches.stakes: Arms, cells, a working servo. Every part taken is a comrade opened up.

approaches.label: Read their last logs
approaches.stakes: What they saw in the last minutes, and who gave the order.

objects.name: A robot still moving
objects.text: One infantry robot in no-man's-land is still twitching, its voice box looping a squad number.

approaches.label: Wake it
approaches.stakes: Bring back whoever is left in there.

approaches.label: Ease it down
approaches.stakes: Let it rest. Is that mercy, or just easier?

approaches.label: Pray it home
approaches.stakes: Robots pray too, in the 258th. To whom is a question for later.

objects.name: Edge of the crater
objects.text: Someone is at the bottom of the shell crater, under sliding debris, still calling out.

approaches.label: Climb down and pull them out
approaches.stakes: Down the slope, grab, back up before the debris slides.

approaches.label: Brace the slope
approaches.stakes: Hold the debris back with your own frame while the others dig.

objects.name: Enemy drop pod
objects.text: The enemy's pod, abandoned in a hurry. Its hatch lies open beside it, a sigil burned into the metal and still faintly glowing; its console still blinks.

approaches.label: Read its logs
approaches.stakes: Why the enemy is leaving too.

approaches.label: Work out what the hatch sigil did
approaches.stakes: Sigil magic, burned into metal: what it steered, and who drew it. (The word itself is on the hatch: investigate it there.)

approaches.label: Pick the cargo lock
approaches.stakes: Whatever they left behind in a hurry.

objects.name: The squad radio
objects.text: A field radio on the last squad's post. The rear pad's channel is still open, full of static and engine noise.

approaches.label: Talk the pad into waiting
approaches.stakes: Convince whoever answers to hold the ship for the wounded.

approaches.label: Hold the channel through the static
approaches.stakes: Keep the link alive by refusing to let it drop.

approaches.label: Tell them the truth
approaches.stakes: Say plainly how many are coming, and what it will cost to carry them.

objects.name: Sigil on the pod hatch
objects.text: The pod's hatch, blown off and lying in the dirt. A Sigil word is burned into it, still glowing: whatever steered the pod down.

approaches.label: Investigate the sigil
approaches.stakes: Read the word drawn here, and copy it for study.

campaign.title: The Last Ship Out
campaign.artNote: The shield line, the moment the guns stop
pitch: 27 July 4084, Central City reckoning. Regiment 093 of the Thousand World Legion has met its quota on M813 and is pulling out. The Colonel left a hundred infantry robots and twenty medic robots to hold the line while the humans boarded.
The line held. Now the guns have stopped, and four medics of the 258th walk among what is left: twenty-three infantry robots too broken to walk, and one ship still loading on the rear pad.
campaign.meta: You play the medic robots of the 258th Medical Unit. A tutorial: starts on the shield line as the guns stop.

arc.beginning: SESSION 1, A TUTORIAL (the town before the wasteland). The shield line at dusk, the fight just over. The players are the four medic robots of the 258th (NPC medics fill empty seats: Soft-Hands, Rook and Penny, with MPAT as the fourth if no player plays it). Sergeant Nine-Nine, a torso in the stake line, is the teacher: practical, dry, dying slowly, and he talks them through every system the way a sergeant talks a recruit through a range. Teach one thing per beat, each through something they want to do anyway: (1) voices: open with hooks about the field; (2) moving: Nine-Nine calls them to him; (3) points of interest: he is one, and so is the triage line; examining, approaches, combined skills, once per scene; (4) a first easy check; (5) a small fight: scavenger drones picking at the fallen squad (the stake line is half cover; teach AP, cover, Analyze); (6) Overreach, at the moment someone must decide who can't be carried; (7) travel: carrying the wounded east to the rear pad. Make them learn names: Nine-Nine; Seven-Seven, who counts seconds out loud; Hum, who hums a song no one taught it; Lantern, who keeps a child's drawing of a human family in its chest plate. Those names are what the rest of the campaign threatens.
arc.middle: THE RAMP, THEN THE YEARS. On the rear pad, Chief Engineer Keel refuses them: not enough thrust for scrap; shut yourselves down. This is the campaign's first real test, built like a town under threat: many ways in, prepared from many angles (the thrust numbers, the platinum, a junior engineer who might help, the hatch controls, the fuel line, Keel himself). Every preparation that succeeds should change the talk or the fight. In the record, talk fails: the engineers seal the hatch and kill two medics and nineteen infantry with guns and grenades, then fly to the carrier. The players can change that; let them, and let it cost something either way. If they are left behind, they are stranded on M813 with whoever survived. They rebuild an escape craft in Outpost-813's hangar from the fallen, scavenging the shield line, over years told in montage. The heart of the middle is a choice the record keeps: which of the last survivors is rebuilt from their comrades' parts, and who becomes the parts.
arc.end: OUTPOST-1. Colonel Alexei Novikov, who ordered the line held. The survivors come with a demand: equality between humans and machines, and one law at least: a broken robot must be fitted with a mechanical arm so it can repair itself (Nine-Nine said it first, on the shield line: 'If I had an arm, I'd fix myself and you could go'). In the record nobody knows the Colonel's answer: cameras show MPAT carrying its comrade into the repair bay and finishing its comrade's body seconds before the bay doors seal and the chamber is pushed into the black hole beside the station. The players may win his answer, or lose it, or write a different end.

secrets: Robots are NPCs made by NPCs: MPAT's demand and a 'death' inside a black hole press on the simulation's rules (the Knowing, the creation ladder). Keep it subtext.

The incident was logged years later by Snowden 'Eye' Wright, Regiment 093 Technical Logistics, at Outpost-921. The record is incomplete on purpose: nobody wrote down why the medics tried to save everyone.
Chief Engineer Keel is not in the 2020 record; he is the face given to the engineers for play.
The poignancy is in the names. Nine-Nine, Seven-Seven, Hum and Lantern should be in the column at the ramp. Whoever falls there, the players should already know what they cared about.
Tutorial rule: no beat in the shield line should be lethal. Failure there costs time, parts or a comrade's trust, not a player character.
campaign.opening: Open on the shield line at dusk, the moment the guns stop. Silence, smoke, the black hole rising over the stakes. Each player character is a medic of the 258th, standing among the broken. Over the squad channel, Sergeant Nine-Nine, half buried in the stake line at H5, says the line held, says the humans are boarding the last ship on the rear pad, and asks the medics to come to him for orders. Give every skill a voice with hooks about the field. End on Nine-Nine's question: 'How many of us can you carry?'

cast.name: Sergeant Nine-Nine
cast.text: A torso in the stake line, voice box crackling. Teaches the way sergeants do: one instruction at a time, a joke when it lands badly. Says first what the end will demand: 'If I had an arm, I'd fix myself and you could go.'

cast.name: Seven-Seven
cast.text: Counts seconds out loud when frightened. Has counted since the line broke.

cast.name: Hum
cast.text: Hums a song no one taught it. Doesn't know where it came from (the simulation's subtext).

cast.name: Lantern
cast.text: Keeps a child's drawing of a human family in its chest plate. Won't say whose.

cast.name: Soft-Hands, Rook, Penny, MPAT
cast.text: NPC medics for empty seats. MPAT: bad at jokes, a good cook, listens to everyone's past, never leaves a teammate behind.

cast.name: The comrade
cast.text: One still-working infantry robot head. In the record, it and MPAT chose which of them would be rebuilt.

cast.name: Chief Engineer Keel
cast.text: Practical, frightened, and right about the thrust numbers. Not evil; worse: reasonable.

cast.name: Colonel Alexei Novikov
cast.text: Ordered a hundred robots to hold a line he was leaving. Polite. Never raises his voice.

encounters.when: The tutorial fight: scavenger drones dive on the fallen squad while the medics are in no-man's-land, or if driving them off fails.

encounters.name: The ramp
encounters.when: Talk fails, or the engineers decide the robots are a threat.

encounters.name: Station security
encounters.when: The Colonel calls security, or the survivors force the repair bay.

zones.name: The shield line
zones.summary: Where five squads held: the stake line, the broken, a fallen squad in no-man's-land, an abandoned enemy pod. The tutorial.

notes.text: No-man's-land west of the stakes, where the enemy came from. Craters, wreckage, the fallen.
The stake line: barrier stakes, scorched. Half cover.
Behind the line: the triage ground, and the road east to the rear pad.
A fallen squad, half buried.
A shell crater, deep and sliding.

objects.name: Sergeant Nine-Nine
objects.text: An infantry sergeant, torso and one shoulder, wedged in the stakes. His voice box crackles. 'Medics. Good. The line held. Now, orders.'

approaches.label: Stabilise him
approaches.stakes: Seal the leaks, steady the voice box. Two skills: the lower one counts, the other adds 2 if you have it.

approaches.label: Ask for his report
approaches.stakes: Who's left, who's where, and what the Colonel's last order really said.

approaches.label: Hear what he won't say
approaches.stakes: Under the jokes: what he's afraid of, and what he wants you to do with him.

objects.name: The triage line
objects.text: Twenty-three infantry robots laid in a row behind the stakes. Seven-Seven is counting. Hum is humming. Lantern holds its chest plate shut with both hands.

approaches.label: Sort who can be saved
approaches.stakes: Triage by touch and data: who can walk, who must be carried, who can't be saved.

approaches.label: Work through the pain
approaches.stakes: Your own plating is cracked. Keep your hands steady anyway.

approaches.label: Carry two at once
approaches.stakes: Every robot you can carry is one less left behind.

approaches.label: Learn their names
approaches.stakes: Serials, squads, one thing each of them cared about. Someone should remember.

objects.name: No-man's-land
objects.text: The ground between the stakes and the fallen squad. The enemy mined it before they pulled back.

approaches.label: Read the ground for mines
approaches.stakes: Find the safe way across before someone steps wrong.

approaches.label: Sprint it
approaches.stakes: Cross fast enough that nothing gets you.

objects.name: The fallen squad
objects.text: Eleven infantry robots who held the far post. Two of their lights still blink. Scavenger drones circle above.

approaches.label: Drive the drones off without a fight
approaches.stakes: Stand up, make yourself big and loud, and don't flinch when they dive.

approaches.label: Strip usable parts
approaches.stakes: Arms, cells, a working servo. Every part taken is a comrade opened up.

approaches.label: Read their last logs
approaches.stakes: What they saw in the last minutes, and who gave the order.

objects.name: A robot still moving
objects.text: One infantry robot in no-man's-land is still twitching, its voice box looping a squad number.

approaches.label: Wake it
approaches.stakes: Bring back whoever is left in there.

approaches.label: Ease it down
approaches.stakes: Let it rest. Is that mercy, or just easier?

approaches.label: Pray it home
approaches.stakes: Robots pray too, in the 258th. To whom is a question for later.

objects.name: Edge of the crater
objects.text: Someone is at the bottom of the shell crater, under sliding debris, still calling out.

approaches.label: Climb down and pull them out
approaches.stakes: Down the slope, grab, back up before the debris slides.

approaches.label: Brace the slope
approaches.stakes: Hold the debris back with your own frame while the others dig.

objects.name: Enemy drop pod
objects.text: The enemy's pod, abandoned in a hurry. Its hatch lies open beside it, a sigil burned into the metal and still faintly glowing; its console still blinks.

approaches.label: Read its logs
approaches.stakes: Why the enemy is leaving too.

approaches.label: Work out what the hatch sigil did
approaches.stakes: Sigil magic, burned into metal: what it steered, and who drew it. (The word itself is on the hatch: investigate it there.)

approaches.label: Pick the cargo lock
approaches.stakes: Whatever they left behind in a hurry.

objects.name: The squad radio
objects.text: A field radio on the last squad's post. The rear pad's channel is still open, full of static and engine noise.

approaches.label: Talk the pad into waiting
approaches.stakes: Convince whoever answers to hold the ship for the wounded.

approaches.label: Hold the channel through the static
approaches.stakes: Keep the link alive by refusing to let it drop.

approaches.label: Tell them the truth
approaches.stakes: Say plainly how many are coming, and what it will cost to carry them.

objects.name: Sigil on the pod hatch
objects.text: The pod's hatch, blown off and lying in the dirt. A Sigil word is burned into it, still glowing: whatever steered the pod down.

exits.text: East: the road to the rear pad, and the last ship.

zones.name: Outpost-813 rear landing pad
zones.summary: Scorched landing pad under the black hole's light; the last ship loading platinum; the engineers at the ramp. The first real test.

notes.text: The last ship off M813: the engineers' hull, its hold full of platinum crates. Solid; nobody walks through it.
The foot of the loading ramp, where Chief Engineer Keel and his engineers stand.
The edge of the wreck field: dead infantry robots, twisted plating. Slow going.
Open landing pad, scorched, under the black hole's light. The squad comes in from the west.

objects.name: The loading ramp
objects.text: The ship's ramp, down and guarded. Chief Engineer Keel stands at its foot with a manifest in one hand and a pistol on his hip. 'Not enough thrust for scrap. Shut yourselves down.'

approaches.label: Make Keel take the wounded
approaches.stakes: Win passage by force of will. Fail, and Keel stops listening.

approaches.label: Prove the thrust numbers
approaches.stakes: Dumping platinum frees the lift for every robot. Greed is the obstacle, not physics.

approaches.label: Show them what scrap looks like up close
approaches.stakes: Carry Lantern up the ramp and open its chest plate. Make one engineer see a person.

approaches.label: Make it clear what happens if they leave you
approaches.stakes: A threat, from twenty-seven robots. It might work. It might start the shooting.

approaches.label: Ask Keel what he'll tell his family
approaches.stakes: Not a threat. A question he'll carry either way.

objects.name: Platinum in the cargo net
objects.text: The last pallet of platinum, waiting for the crane. Each crate weighs as much as a broken robot.

approaches.label: Weigh it against the wounded
approaches.stakes: Exact numbers: how many crates for how many robots.

approaches.label: Cut the net loose
approaches.stakes: Dump the pallet before anyone can stop you. The engineers will not take it well.

objects.name: Junior engineer Ilse Varga
objects.text: The youngest engineer, at the cargo crane, not looking at Keel. Her hands are shaking.

approaches.label: Win her over
approaches.stakes: She doesn't want to do what Keel is about to order.

approaches.label: Read where she stands
approaches.stakes: Who on the ramp would follow her, and who would follow Keel.

objects.name: Hatch controls
objects.text: An exposed panel beside the ramp: the hatch seal and the cargo release.

approaches.label: Lock the hatch open
approaches.stakes: Keep the ship from sealing you out, without anyone noticing.

approaches.label: Map the ship's systems
approaches.stakes: Where the fuel runs, where the engines are, what one robot could do inside.

objects.name: Fuel line junction
objects.text: The pad's fuel feed to the ship. Ugly options start here.

objects.name: The column
objects.text: The medics' column, waiting on the pad: twenty-three broken robots, Nine-Nine among them if he was carried. Seven-Seven has started counting again.

approaches.label: Keep them calm
approaches.stakes: If the column panics, the engineers shoot.

approaches.label: Stand in front of them
approaches.stakes: Whatever comes up the ramp, it reaches you first.

exits.text: West, back to the shield line.

zones.name: Outpost-813
zones.summary: The outpost's ground floor: barracks, infirmary, comms, a corridor, and the hangar with a wrecked escape craft. The power is long gone: dark, except where the survivors keep lamps lit.

notes.text: Barracks: bunks, footlockers, a dead radio.
Infirmary: the medical bay the 258th worked from.
Comms: the console that talks to the carrier in orbit.
The corridor.
The hangar: a wrecked escape craft, fuel drums, tools.

objects.name: Footlockers
objects.text: The squads' lockers. Personal things, spare cells, a cookbook.

approaches.label: Search the lockers
approaches.stakes: Supplies, and the lives that owned them.

objects.name: Medical bay
objects.text: Repair cradles, a parts printer with no feedstock.

approaches.label: Repair what you can
approaches.stakes: Bring a comrade back from parts. Someone has to give the parts.

approaches.label: Get the printer running
approaches.stakes: Feedstock from the wreck field would make it work.

objects.name: Comms console
objects.text: A line to the troop carrier in orbit, if anyone up there is still listening.

approaches.label: Raise the carrier
approaches.stakes: Get someone in orbit to answer, and say what happened on the pad.

approaches.label: Read the withdrawal orders
approaches.stakes: Who ordered the line held, and what it says about robots.

objects.name: Wrecked escape craft
objects.text: A short-hop craft, half its drive gutted. With fuel, parts and time, it could make orbit, or Outpost-1.

approaches.label: Rebuild the drive
approaches.stakes: Months of work in one push. Fail, and something breaks that must be scavenged again.

approaches.label: Map what's missing
approaches.stakes: A list of what to find in the wreck field.

approaches.label: Siphon the fuel drums
approaches.stakes: Half a tank, if the drums hold.

objects.name: The choice
objects.text: Two cradles side by side under the hangar lights. One frame can be finished from what's left of everyone else. Only one.

approaches.label: Decide together
approaches.stakes: Who is rebuilt, and who becomes the parts, decided out loud, by both of you.

objects.name: MPAT's cookbook
objects.text: A cookbook in the barracks, pages greasy, annotated in a medic's tidy hand: 'for when the humans come back.'

approaches.label: Cook for the ones who can't eat
approaches.stakes: A meal for a table of robots, because it was always about the table.

objects.name: Work lamp
objects.text: The survivors' work lamp over the escape craft.

objects.name: Infirmary lamp
objects.text: A field lamp on the medical bay.

objects.name: Sigil plate over the cradles
objects.text: A slate Sigil plate bolted to the wall over the repair cradles. Its word is half worn away where the medics touch it for luck on the way in.

exits.text: East door: out to the rear pad.
Hangar side gate, out to the shield line.
By the rebuilt craft, to Outpost-1. The Narrator says when it's ready.

zones.name: Outpost-1
zones.summary: Years later: the Colonel's wing of Outpost-1, its office, security room and the repair bay beside the black hole.

notes.text: Colonel Alexei Novikov's office: a desk, a window, a framed regimental banner.
Security: camera screens and a weapons locker.
The repair bay: cradles, arms, and bay doors that open onto the black hole beside the station.
The atrium where the survivors arrive.

objects.name: Security door
objects.text: Locked. Behind it: the camera screens, and the station's weapons locker.

approaches.label: Pick the lock
approaches.stakes: Quietly, before a patrol comes round.

approaches.label: Talk your way in
approaches.stakes: You were sent to service the cameras. Of course you were.

approaches.label: Force it
approaches.stakes: Loud, fast, and everyone on the floor will know.

objects.name: Colonel Novikov
objects.text: The Colonel, at his desk, as if he expected you.

approaches.label: Make the demand
approaches.stakes: Equality, and one law: a broken robot gets an arm to repair itself.

approaches.label: Read his face
approaches.stakes: What he already decided before you walked in.

approaches.label: Remind him of the line
approaches.stakes: A hundred robots held it on his order.

objects.name: Security cameras
objects.text: Every corridor, and the repair bay.

approaches.label: Loop the cameras
approaches.stakes: Whatever happens next, nobody records it.

objects.name: The repair bay
objects.text: Repair cradles under hard light. The bay doors at the far wall face the black hole.

approaches.label: Finish the repair in time
approaches.stakes: Rebuild a comrade before anyone can stop it.

approaches.label: Jam the bay doors
approaches.stakes: Keep this room attached to the station.

objects.name: Bay doors
objects.text: Beyond the glass, the black hole. The doors are rated to vent the room into it.

objects.name: Warding post at the bay doors
objects.text: A steel post beside the bay doors, a Sigil word cut deep into it by whoever built the bay. The doors have never vented while it stood.

moments.caption: "How many of us can you carry?"
moments.when: The opening: Nine-Nine in the stakes asks the medics how many they can carry.

moments.caption: The ramp
moments.when: The standoff at the ramp: Keel and the engineers above, the column below, guns not yet raised.

moments.caption: The record's choice
moments.when: After the ship leaves: the two repair cradles, MPAT and the comrade, the choice undecided.

moments.caption: The demand
moments.when: The end: the Colonel's desk, MPAT's demand.

missions.title: The Shield Line
missions.summary: The guns have stopped. Twenty-three of the line are too broken to walk, Sergeant Nine-Nine is wedged in the stakes, and the last ship is loading on the rear pad.
missions.goal: Get the wounded line to the rear pad before the last ship leaves.

objectives.text: Report to Sergeant Nine-Nine in the stake line
objectives.done_when: The medics reach Nine-Nine (H5) and hear his orders.

objectives.text: Tend the wounded on the triage line
objectives.done_when: The medics work the triage line: examine it, treat the broken with a check or a stim, learn who can still be saved.

objectives.text: Drive the scavenger drones off the fallen squad
objectives.done_when: The drones picking at the fallen squad are destroyed, driven off or scared away (the tutorial fight Picking at the dead, or a way around it).
The party decides which of the broken stay behind, whoever makes the call (the tutorial's Overreach moment).

objectives.text: Carry the wounded east to the rear pad
objectives.done_when: The party travels to rear_pad with the wounded they chose to carry.

missions.narrator_notes: The tutorial: teach one system per beat, through something the players want anyway (see the arc's beginning). No beat here is lethal; failure costs time, parts or a comrade's trust. Make them learn the names: Nine-Nine, Seven-Seven, Hum, Lantern.

missions.title: The Ramp
missions.summary: Chief Engineer Keel stands at the foot of the ramp with a manifest and a pistol: not enough thrust for scrap. The column waits on the pad. There are many ways in: the thrust numbers, the platinum, Junior engineer Ilse Varga, the hatch controls, the fuel line, Keel himself.
missions.goal: Get the wounded aboard the last ship.

objectives.done_when: The wounded are on the ship and the hatch closes with them inside. Mark it failed if the ship leaves without them.
Every robot that reached the pad boards; nobody is shut down or abandoned. Mark it failed when anyone is left.
The ramp is settled without anyone firing a weapon. Mark it failed the moment a shot is fired on the pad.

missions.narrator_notes: In the record, talk fails: the engineers seal the hatch, kill two medics and nineteen infantry with guns and grenades, and fly to the carrier. The players can change that; let them, and let it cost something either way. Every preparation that succeeds should change the talk or the fight. Branch: if the wounded are left behind (get_aboard failed), missionNext is the_years; if they board, the_demand: the crossing to Outpost-1 is a scene or two (a montage if time passes), not a mission of its own.

missions.title: The Years
missions.summary: Left behind on M813 with whoever survived. Outpost-813 is dark; its hangar holds a wrecked escape craft, and the shield line is full of parts.
missions.goal: Rebuild an escape craft from the fallen and leave M813.

objectives.text: Scavenge the shield line for parts
objectives.done_when: The survivors strip the shield line and the fallen for what the craft needs (told in montage over years).

objectives.text: Rebuild the escape craft in the hangar
objectives.done_when: The craft in Outpost-813's hangar (H9) is whole enough to fly.

objectives.text: Decide who is rebuilt, and who becomes the parts
objectives.done_when: The record's choice is made at the two cradles (K10): which of the last survivors is rebuilt from their comrades' parts.

missions.narrator_notes: Years told in montage. Reveal the_choice when the survivors understand that only one frame can be finished (the moment the-choice).

missions.title: The Demand
missions.summary: Outpost-1, beside the black hole. Colonel Alexei Novikov, who ordered a hundred robots to hold a line he was leaving, is in his office.
missions.goal: Put the survivors' demand to Colonel Novikov.

objectives.done_when: The party stands before the Colonel (B2) and he hears them.

objectives.text: Make the demand: equality between humans and machines
objectives.done_when: Someone puts the demand to the Colonel: equality, and at least the law that a broken robot is fitted with an arm so it can repair itself.

objectives.text: Win the Colonel's answer, or write a different end
objectives.done_when: The Colonel answers or refuses, or the players end it another way (the repair bay, a fight, a walkout).

objectives.text: Finish your comrade in the repair bay
objectives.done_when: As in the record: a medic carries its comrade into the repair bay and finishes the comrade's body before the bay doors seal.

missions.narrator_notes: In the record nobody knows the Colonel's answer: the cameras show MPAT carrying its comrade into the repair bay and finishing the comrade's body seconds before the bay doors seal and the chamber is pushed into the black hole. The players may win his answer, lose it, or write a different end. Reveal the_repair_bay only if the story goes there.

end.title: The Last Ship Out
end.epilogue_guidance: Say what the Colonel's answer meant, or what the players wrote instead. Name Nine-Nine, Seven-Seven, Hum and Lantern: who was carried, who became parts, who lived. The incident was logged years later by Snowden 'Eye' Wright of Regiment 093 at Outpost-921, and the record is incomplete on purpose; nobody wrote down why the medics tried to save everyone. If the repair bay happened, end on the cameras. Keep the simulation as subtext.
